title: Authentication & Session Design: Cookies, Refresh Token Rotation & Replay Detection
concept: Design sign-in that holds up under real traffic and real attackers: where the session lives, cookie flags that matter, short-lived access tokens, refresh tokens stored as hashes and rotated in families, replay detection, revocation per device, CSRF and XSS, and two refresh requests that arrive at the same time.
description: An advanced course for backend developers who own a login flow. Every lesson starts from an incident on the CodeDev learning platform - a refresh token copied from a database backup that still worked, a cookie the browser sent to every subdomain, a learner signed out on all devices when one phone refreshed twice in parallel, a stolen refresh token used once more after the real user had rotated it, an AI-written cookie helper that let any script read the token - and fixes it with a design you can test: sessions versus tokens, cookie flags, signing and verifying access tokens with a fake clock, hashing and rotating refresh tokens, token families and replay detection, revoking one device or all of them, CSRF and XSS, concurrent refresh with compare-and-swap, and a threat review. 12 lessons with True/False quizzes on real headers, logs and code, and TypeScript challenges graded by hidden tests.

learningOutcomes.text: Design an access and refresh token flow with short-lived, verified access tokens
Choose where the session lives and set cookie flags that keep tokens away from scripts and other sites
Store refresh tokens as hashes, rotate them in families and revoke one device or all devices
Reduce CSRF, XSS and token replay risk, and detect a replayed refresh token
Handle two refresh requests at the same time without double success or false replay alarms

knownIssues: No PostgreSQL or Redis in the code runner: token stores are in-memory fakes with compare-and-swap that mirror the SQL shown in the lessons
